This outlook stems from an anticipated reduction in capital flowing from foreign investors into Japanese markets, such as stocks and bonds. Conversely, a reduction in foreign investment might imply less selling of yen to buy foreign assets, or potentially increased domestic buying of yen, supporting its value.

card.plain_headline: UBS Forecasts Higher Global Rates to Hurt Swedish Krona
card.what_happened: Analysts at UBS predict that rising global interest rates will put downward pressure on the Swedish Krona (SEK).
card.what_happened_verbose: UBS, a major global financial institution, has issued a forecast indicating that the Swedish Krona is likely to weaken. This prediction is based on the expectation of higher global interest rates. When global interest rates rise, capital tends to flow towards economies offering higher yields, often denominated in stronger currencies. If Sweden's rates do not keep pace or if its economy is perceived as less attractive relative to others, the Krona could see reduced demand. This outflow of capital or reduced inflow can lead to a depreciation of the Krona against other major currencies.
